refined_question: Fix a positive integer r. Using the RSK algorithm coming from the degree-r differential lattice of Young diagrams with at most r rows, which maps r-colored permutations to pairs of tableaux of common bounded-row shape with suitable weighting, determine the asymptotic behavior, as the size tends to infinity, of the resulting Young-diagram shapes, and from that asymptotic identify a scaling under which these bounded-row Young diagrams admit a well-defined limit-shape theory parallel to the classical theory for ordinary Young diagrams. ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))
justification: Problem 6 is the exact target because it is the only place in the paper that asks for a limit-shape theory for Young diagrams with at most r rows and explicitly says that the initial obstacle is to study the asymptotics of the shapes produced by r-colored permutations in order to choose the right scaling. Problem 4 supplies the intended mechanism generating those shapes: the lattice of Young diagrams with at most r rows is differential of degree r, so the general theory gives an RSK algorithm from r-colored permutations to pairs of such tableaux with suitable weighting. Problem 5 explains what "a similar theory of limit shapes" means in this notebook by recalling the classical rescaled Young-diagram limit-shape setup. ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))
